key_insight: HCM-PhenotypeNet combines echocardiography video and clinical data to automatically sort hypertrophic cardiomyopathy patients into four clinically meaningful phenotypes.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help clinicians recognize heterogeneous HCM subgroups for more personalized risk stratification and follow-up, especially for obstructive disease, genotype-positive disease, late-onset mild disease, and heart-failure–predominant disease.
method: Deep neural network extracted features from 1,553 echocardiography video clips.
More than 100 clinical variables from 156 HCM patients were fused into patient-level representations.
UMAP dimensionality reduction and Deep Embedded Clustering (DEC) identified phenotype groups.
evidence_signal: In 156 patients, the best model produced four clusters with strong separation (silhouette about 0.89) and clinically distinct phenogroups.
watch_item: The findings come from a small single-cohort study and need external validation before clinical use.
paper_title: HCM-PhenotypeNet: Deep Multimodal Phenotyping of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy from Echocardiographic Video and Clinical Data
